URL: https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/andy-burnham-greater-manchester-england-keir-starmer-john-healey-b1290860.html
NOTE: Evening Standard/PA (David Hughes, 22 Jul) — "partly funded through changes to international climate finance schemes." Cap in place throughout 2027, reverses £3 increase set by Starmer/Reeves in 2024. Chancellor John Healey: "We are capping bus fares at £2 for everyone throughout 2027, slashing fares by a third for millions of people, to help give them the breathing space they need. This action to ease the cost of living is funded by savings made elsewhere, so there's no burden to British taxpayers, just pounds going back into their pockets." Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander: move would make "everyday journeys easier and cheaper... cutting fares by a third"; "today's move will stop prices jumping next Spring and lower fares to £2 from January... giving local authorities more time to plan with confidence." Funding: extra £454m (incl devolved govts) from reprioritisation of DESNZ budget, switching international climate finance projects into loans.
